description: A junior Computer Science major aiming for a career in software engineering who is mathematically confident but feels intimidated by low-level memory management in C.

nodes.description: Introduction to Operating System services, kernel/user mode, and the architecture of modern operating systems.
nodes.title: OS Foundations and Structures
nodes.personalizationRationale: This node establishes the fundamental structural knowledge required for all students, aligning with the some_prior_exposure tier's need for a standardized conceptual baseline.

nodes.description: A refresher on C-based system calls and environment setup to bridge the gap between general programming and systems programming.
nodes.title: C Systems Programming Refresher
nodes.personalizationRationale: For a student with some_prior_exposure, this single scaffolding node provides a targeted review of C-specific systems integration to ensure readiness for upcoming programming projects.

nodes.description: Exploration of the process lifecycle, PCB (Process Control Block), and the mechanics of process creation and termination.
nodes.title: Process Lifecycle and Operations
nodes.personalizationRationale: A core understanding of the process abstraction is essential for some_prior_exposure students to progress toward complex inter-process communication.
Standard IPC mastery is required for this tier to ensure effective implementation of the subsequent multi-process programming projects.
nodes.title: IPC: Shared Memory and Message Passing
nodes.description: Deep dive into Inter-Process Communication (IPC) via shared memory and message passing protocols.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Given some_prior_exposure, this node builds on basic process knowledge to introduce more efficient concurrency models.
nodes.title: Threading Models and Libraries
nodes.description: Comparison of kernel-level and user-level threading models and introduction to the Pthreads library.
Detailed analysis of CPU scheduling algorithms including FCFS, SJF, and Round Robin.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Understanding the trade-offs in scheduling policies is a core requirement for all students and is heavily tested on the midterm.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Criteria and Algorithms
Midterm Review: Chapters 1-5
nodes.personalizationRationale: This assessment node ensures that the student with some_prior_exposure is fully prepared for the weighted midterm examination.
nodes.description: A comprehensive review of chapters 1 through 5, focusing on foundations, processes, threads, and scheduling in preparation for the midterm.
Introduction to race conditions, critical sections, and the implementation of mutex locks and semaphores.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Synchronization is a foundational OS concept that the student must master regardless of their some_prior_exposure background.
nodes.title: Synchronization Primitives

nodes.description: Applying synchronization primitives to classic problems like the Dining Philosophers and Readers-Writers.
nodes.title: Classic Problems of Synchronization
nodes.personalizationRationale: These classic problems are a staple of OS examinations and provide practical context for some_prior_exposure students.
Providing an enrichment node here challenges students with some_prior_exposure to think about software engineering design patterns in OS.
nodes.title: Advanced Concurrency: Monitors
nodes.description: Analysis of high-level synchronization constructs like monitors and their use in complex systems.

nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization and Detection
nodes.personalizationRationale: Deadlock management is a mandatory module required for the final cumulative examination for all students.
nodes.description: Understanding the four necessary conditions for deadlock and methods for prevention, avoidance, and detection.
Exploration of physical memory allocation, fragmentation, and the implementation of paging and page tables.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This node covers required memory management theory that some_prior_exposure students must master for the final project.
nodes.title: Main Memory and Paging Structures

nodes.description: Detailed study of virtual memory, demand paging, and various page replacement algorithms like LRU and Optimal.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Virtual memory is a heavily tested topic and project-relevant for students in the some_prior_exposure tier.
nodes.title: Virtual Memory and Page Replacement
I/O Subsystems and Performance
nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard I/O knowledge is essential for the student's holistic understanding of OS hardware-software interaction.
nodes.description: Introduction to the I/O subsystem, including interrupts, DMA, and the standard kernel I/O interface.

nodes.title: File System Implementation
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core capstone content is necessary for the student to understand the full stack of OS functionality.
nodes.description: Understanding how file systems are implemented on disk and the trade-offs between different allocation methods.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This cumulative review ensures that students with some_prior_exposure have synthesized all course objectives before the final exam.
nodes.title: Final Cumulative Review
nodes.description: A final, cumulative review session covering all course material from process management through file systems.
